candidates.src: StatCan 10-10-0024-01 — CCOFOG by general government component
candidates.universe: Provincial and territorial governments ONLY (also 7 other components separately)
candidates.classif: CCOFOG functional — but only the 10 top-level divisions at provincial level
candidates.split: Partly — 10 divisions, no Debt or Transport row
candidates.note: Matches the money being allocated exactly. NOT consolidated (FN 3): inter-component transfers are not eliminated, so a provincial grant to a hospital is counted in both components. FN 4 advises against comparing provinces on a single component.

candidates.src: StatCan 10-10-0005-01 — CCOFOG by CONSOLIDATED government component
candidates.universe: Consolidated provincial-territorial and local governments (PTLG) — the only sub-national series
candidates.classif: CCOFOG functional, all 60 members incl. sub-functions
candidates.split: Yes, in full detail — but for the wrong universe
candidates.note: This is the table the app cites. Its sub-national universe consolidates municipalities, school boards, hospitals and universities, so it answers a different question than 'where does my provincial income tax go'. StatCan nevertheless recommends it for inter-provincial comparison, because delegation to municipalities differs by province. That tension is a product decision, not a data one.

candidates.src: StatCan 10-10-0017-01 — CGFS for provincial and territorial governments
candidates.split: No — but supplies the debt carve-out
candidates.note: Same universe, agency and vintage as 10-10-0024-01, so subtracting its Interest expense from CCOFOG division 701 is a same-basis operation. This is the ONE legitimate carve-out available.

candidates.classif: FMS functional — Transportation and communication, Debt charges, Health, Education (elem-sec vs postsec), Social services, Environment, Housing, Protection of persons and property, Recreation and culture
candidates.split: Yes — this is almost exactly the app's taxonomy
candidates.note: The single most important finding for framing. The app's ten categories are FMS-shaped and were sourceable at provincial level until StatCan retired FMS for CCOFOG. All lines populated 21 of 21 years for Ontario. The taxonomy was inherited, not invented — but it can no longer be sourced.

candidates.src: Finances of the Nation (Canadian Tax Foundation)
candidates.universe: Federal + all 13 provinces/territories; carries an Include_Local flag, so provincial-only AND provincial-plus-local both available
candidates.classif: Only THREE expenditure lines: Total expenditure, Program expenditure, Debt charges
candidates.split: NO — verified by enumerating every item id in the 35MB CSV
candidates.verdict: BEST NON-STATCAN SOURCE, BUT CANNOT SPLIT
candidates.note: Built explicitly for cross-jurisdiction comparability, CC-licensed, and the only source found that bridges the 2009 FMS/CCOFOG discontinuity. Public Accounts basis. Use it as an independent second measure of the debt row and as a long-run sanity check — not for the allocation.

candidates.universe: By province/territory, broken out by source of finance incl. provincial government specifically
candidates.verdict: BEST CHECK ON THE HEALTH ROW
candidates.note: Health is ~40% of the provincial pie, so an independent measure of that single row is worth more than an independent measure of most others combined.

candidates.classif: Economic: transfers to persons, transfers to business, interest on public debt, transfers to other levels of government
candidates.cover: Long run, both Public Accounts and National Accounts basis
candidates.note: Publishing both bases makes it useful for checking whether a Public Accounts figure and a National Accounts figure ought to agree.

candidates.src: RBC — Canadian Federal and Provincial Fiscal Tables
candidates.classif: Budget-balance oriented, compiled from the 13 public accounts and budgets
candidates.note: RBC states outright that its figures 'are not strictly comparable between provinces'. Convenient way to locate the underlying public accounts; not an authority.
Revenue, expenditure and budgetary balance only.
